cases.question: How should five certain trump winners and eight unestablished hearts affect bidding and the order of suit development?
cases.observed: Maya bids9 and interleaves two trump rounds, another heart lead, a trump entry and a final trump lead.
cases.fact: Each of Maya's five top spades must win its own trick in this ruleset; extra heart tricks depend on the remaining distribution and play.
cases.exception: A heart-void opponent with longer trump can outlast the draw; partner's ruffs or Nil may change the cost of drawing.
cases.nextTest: Fresh complete continuations across companion deals, bids and seating; no hidden-distribution label in the player's input.
cases.coachCandidate: Count five trump winners; test whether the hearts can become winners.

cases.question: How does reaching the contract change the value of retaining honors?
cases.observed: Leo has made his bid and seeks to avoid bags; Jason still needs a trick.
cases.exception: A completed personal contract does not by itself establish the best match-level action; setting opponents and future bag thresholds matter.
cases.nextTest: Replay this public shape with changed scores, bags and contract needs; use the exact variant scorer.
cases.coachCandidate: Compare your remaining contract need with the effect on opponents.

cases.question: When can public voids and card counts disprove a future winning route?
cases.observed: Jason still describes his queens as potential winners after the sweep is provable, then recognizes it later.
cases.fact: records/public-proof.json proves the six-heart sweep from Jason's seq31 packet alone.
cases.exception: An unaccounted trump or an unproved club/diamond void invalidates this proof; the earlier seq23 packet does not prove it.
cases.nextTest: Attach explicit premises to explanation claims; add reachable counterexamples with retained trump or another lead route.
cases.coachCandidate: The remaining hearts control the hand; your queens cannot gain the lead.

cases.question: Should the coach distinguish between outcome-equivalent discards?
cases.fact: After the public sweep proof, these defenders cannot alter the remaining trick winners with any legal discard.
cases.exception: Do not generalize rank equivalence when a remaining suit entry or trump can change control.
cases.nextTest: Mark the acceptable action set, test a counterexample, and suppress repeated cues when no meaningful choice remains.
cases.coachCandidate: Several discards have the same result.
